rules.title: Cartwright Act: prohibition on use or distribution of common pricing algorithms (AB 325)
rules.requirement: It is unlawful to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, trust or conspiracy to restrain trade. It is also unlawful to use or distribute one while coercing another person to adopt a price or commercial term it recommends for the same or similar products or services in California.
rules.key_value: Ban on using or distributing a 'common pricing algorithm' (any methodology, including software, used by two or more persons that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set or influence a price or commercial term) in restraint of trade or with coercion to adopt its recommendations.
rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.coverage_text: Any person (as defined in Section 16702, excluding the end consumer of a product or service) who uses or distributes a common pricing algorithm, meaning any methodology, including a computer, software, or other technology, used by two or more persons, that uses competitor data to recommend, align, stabilize, set, or otherwise influence a price or commercial term. Commercial term includes level of service, availability and output. Distribution includes selling, licensing, providing access to, or making available by any means, including by subscription.
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to the end consumer of a product or service, who is excluded from the definition of 'person'.
rules.penalty: Violation is a violation of the Cartwright Act, which the digest states is punishable as a crime. The section does not limit other antitrust remedies.
rules.interaction: Added to the Cartwright Act. Nothing in § 16729 impairs or limits the applicability of other antitrust laws. New § 16756.1 lowers the pleading standard for any Cartwright Act complaint: it suffices to allege facts making a contract, trust or conspiracy plausible, and the complaint need not allege facts excluding the possibility of independent action.
rules.extraction_note: The statute is economy-wide and does not mention rental housing specifically. It is classified as algorithmic_rent_setting because it covers pricing software that uses competitor data to set prices, which would include rent. The text gives no effective date, so effective_date is left blank. Status in_force is assumed from the chaptered/approved status (approved by Governor and filed with Secretary of State 2025-10-06) as of the query date 2026-10-01. The text itself states no effective date.
